Why a stop of its own
This is the only function whose behaviour changes for existing callers, so it gets a stop of
its own, read right after the constructor it depends on.

much was there, and otherwise takes the stock and records the reservation in the log.
A bad request used to wait for the lock before failing, and the old error did not say what
was missing. Recording under the lock keeps the log in the same order as the stock changes.

> [margin q1] inventory/stock.go:39 in station reserve: Does wrapping the error change what callers see?
Only the message. The new error wraps the sentinel with %w, so errors.Is(err, ErrInsufficient) is still true and
callers that branch on it keep working. Nothing in this repository compares with ==, so nothing breaks.
